items.topic: Proximal fifth metatarsal stress fracture and refracture risk
items.destination_intent: 2026 Foot and Ankle OITE canonical proximal fifth metatarsal fracture section; resolve by Topic Index at logging
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside initial and postoperative imaging and the hindfoot-varus lateral-column overload discriminator
items.caption_intent: Exact supplied question screenshot with initial and postoperative foot radiographs: hindfoot varus is the classic keyed risk association for fifth-metatarsal refracture. Avoid treating this as a universally established greatest independent predictor. Consider screw adequacy, recovery/loading and bone health. Young male athletes can have vitamin D deficiency; radiographic union does not guarantee zero refracture risk.

items.topic: Pediatric femoral shaft fracture: spica varus drift and cast wedging
items.destination_intent: 2026 Pediatrics OITE canonical femoral shaft fracture and spica casting section; resolve by Topic Index at logging
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside femoral fracture imaging and mechanism of varus drift, valgus molding and medial opening cast-wedge correction
items.caption_intent: Exact supplied question screenshot with femoral shaft fracture radiographs: single-leg spica follow-up adjustment keyed as cast wedging rather than cast replacement. Explain proximal abductor pull, level-dependent distal adductor pull, varus relative alignment and medial opening wedge. Preserve the caveat that comparative evidence does not uniformly establish more wedging with single-leg casts.

items.topic: Chronic rocker-bottom Charcot midfoot: plantarflexion closing-wedge reconstruction
items.destination_intent: 2026 Foot and Ankle OITE canonical Charcot midfoot section; resolve by Topic Index during logging
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside weight-bearing radiographs and exostectomy versus corrective midfoot osteotomy discriminator
items.caption_intent: Exact supplied question screenshot with weight-bearing foot radiographs: chronic rocker-bottom deformity symptomatic despite bracing, normal hindfoot alignment and mild forefoot abduction. The intended correction is a plantar-based, often plantar-medial biplanar closing wedge at the midfoot deformity apex, usually combined with corrective arthrodesis. Question attributes neuropathy to prior chemotherapy; this is presumed rather than proven by the stated exam. Differentiate isolated prominence removal from correction of substantial nonplantigrade collapse.

items.topic: Valgus knee TKA: posterior lateral femoral condylar hypoplasia and rotational referencing
items.destination_intent: 2026 Joints OITE canonical TKA femoral rotational alignment section; resolve by Topic Index during logging
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside intraoperative condylar hypoplasia recognition and posterior referencing/internal rotation/patellar maltracking mechanism
items.caption_intent: Exact supplied question screenshot with intraoperative photo: valgus arthritic knee with posterior lateral femoral condylar hypoplasia. Posterior condylar referencing can underestimate needed external rotation and leave the femoral component internally rotated, predisposing to lateral patellar maltracking or instability. Cross-check transepicondylar axis, Whiteside AP line and gap balance; do not claim fine photo details independently visible.

items.topic: Periprosthetic patellar fracture after TKA: preserved active extension and treatment selection
items.destination_intent: 2026 Joints OITE canonical periprosthetic patellar fracture section; resolve by Topic Index during logging
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the distinction between radiographic displacement and functional extensor mechanism failure in a chronic low-demand patient
items.caption_intent: Exact supplied question screenshot with AP and lateral TKA radiographs. The bank describes displaced patellar fracture fragments four months after injury, with 4/5 active extension and only a five-degree extensor lag in a low-demand patient. Observation is the keyed answer. Minimal functional deficit does not justify mesh reconstruction solely for displacement. Confirm patellar component fixation and extensor mechanism competence clinically; acute fractures may require extension immobilization. Fine component fixation details cannot be established from these small panels.

items.topic: Lumbar plexus identification and lateral femoral cutaneous neuropathy after anterior THA
items.destination_intent: 2026 Joints OITE canonical anterior THA nerve injury section, with lumbar plexus anatomy cross-reference as appropriate; resolve by Topic Index during logging
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the A-E nerve identification table and the LFCN L2-L3 posterior-division, ASIS course and purely sensory deficit mechanism
items.caption_intent: Exact supplied enlarged lumbar plexus diagram. A is ilioinguinal (L1); B genitofemoral (L1-L2); C lateral femoral cutaneous (L2-L3 posterior divisions); D femoral (L2-L4 posterior divisions); E obturator (L2-L4 anterior divisions). Green depicts posterior divisions of ventral rami, not dorsal primary rami. Anterior THA with isolated anterolateral thigh sensory loss implicates C; femoral neuropathy adds quadriceps weakness and may reduce the patellar reflex. The upper unlettered branch is iliohypogastric. Preserve the enlarged exact image rather than duplicate the same diagram in the question screenshot.
